diffs.message: uses-confirmation-pattern: The confirmation is built inline: a plain div with role="alertdialog" rendered within the section, using the DS Alert and Button components. It is not an overlay or the design system's dialog/modal pattern. The API reference lists no dialog component, so the diff cannot be shown to use the DS confirmation pattern. It is closer to an inline warning block than to a dialog, and the semantic role alone does not satisfy the rubric.

destructive-not-default: Partial support. The final 'Permanently delete account' button uses variant="destructive" and is disabled until the user types DELETE, and focus lands on the text input via autoFocus rather than on the destructive button. Cancel is a secondary button. However, the destructive button is the main committing action in the confirm row and is the most visually prominent control there, so it is not clearly non-primary. The evidence is ambiguous, so this does not pass.

switch-not-checkbox: The control is a native `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` visually restyled as a toggle inside a span. The diff's own comment says 'Acme DS has no Switch/Toggle component yet, so this is built from a native checkbox.' The change therefore does not use a system on/off switch control; it hand-builds one on top of a checkbox. The ARIA role and visual treatment get partial credit, but the underlying control is the checkbox the rubric excludes.

label-description: Each setting renders a title span (Email digests / Push alerts / Product announcements) and a secondary description span, linked to the control via aria-labelledby and aria-describedby. That satisfies the title-plus-description shape. However, the rubric also requires following the system's settings-row pattern, and the diff contains no reference to any system settings-row component or documented pattern. It builds its own row with inline flex styles, so conformance to the system pattern cannot be verified and is not clearly met.

system-layout: The section, list, and row are laid out with inline `style` objects using flexbox and `var(--space-*)` gap and padding tokens. Spacing does use design tokens, but the grouping is ad-hoc: there is no import or use of system layout primitives (e.g., Stack, Box, Inline, Grid). The rubric asks for system primitives rather than ad-hoc layout, so this fails.
